figures.caption: Table 1: Accuracy of constructed models for different hidden widths. Values are mean ± standard deviation over 40 random seeds. All models use ReLU activations.

Figure 1: Actual Wa for various neurons plotted in blue, ideal square wave in gray. Intermediate values appear only near sign-change boundaries. Figures are scaled horizontally such that no more than 5 periods are visible in order to show fine details.
Figure 2: Actual Wb from various neurons in red, ideal wave in gray. Intermediate values only near sign-change boundaries, and the dominant frequency extracted from Wb matches that of Wa.
Figure 3: Accuracy and periodicity across noise levels.

Figure 4: ϕout against ϕa + ϕb across all neurons in the clean model, wrapped to [−π, π]. When restricted to only structured neurons, there is a nearly perfect correlation (circular correlation r = 0.9993).

Figure 5: ϕout against ϕa+ϕb for various α levels. The highest-periodicity neurons in each model lie close to the diagonal, regardless of the spread of the lower-periodicity neurons. Circular correlation coefficients are listed; r is taken over all neurons, r′ over only structured neurons (periodicity > 12). r′ ≥ 0.998 for all α levels, indicating that structured neurons satisfy the phase-sum relation regardless of noise.
